headline: Avoiding Common Kitchen Design Blunders
articleBody: When you're dreaming up a new kitchen, it's easy to get caught up in aesthetics, but sometimes functional pitfalls can sneak in! One big mistake we often see is designing around an idealized vision instead of how you truly live and cook. For example, if you rarely entertain, a huge island might not be as practical as more counter space or dedicated storage. Another common one is underestimating just how much storage you really need – pots, pans, small appliances, pantry items… it adds up fast! It's also easy to forget about crucial countertop space around your prep areas and appliances, or to misjudge where electrical sockets would be most convenient. A big one is not accounting for enough clearance, especially around islands, cabinet doors, and appliances. You need to be able to move freely and open everything without bumping into things. Before you finalize anything, try to visualize yourself using the space. Walk through your daily routine mentally. Will the fridge door block the pathway? Is there enough room to pull out a dishwasher and still stand comfortably? This kind of thinking helps catch those little frustrations before they become big ones. If your project involves moving appliances, changing the entire layout, or dealing with tricky space constraints, that's definitely a time when bringing in a professional can save you a lot of headaches down the road.
